sources.title: ACME E-FIELD Flames — Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments Electric-Field Effects on Laminar Diffusion Flames — approach
sources.text: The experiment is conducted with gas-fueled flames, both with and without a coflow of air. In the former case, the tests are conducted using the same coflow burner used by the Coflow Laminar Diffusion (CLD) Flame experiment. An electric field is generated by creating a high voltage (up to 10 kV) differential between the burner and a flat circular mesh suspended above (i.e., downstream of) the burner. Measurements, as a function of the field strength and fuel, are taken of the ion current through the flame and the flame’s response time to electric forcing.

sources.title: Utilization of the Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment Data for Advanced Modeling and Simulation of Smoke Generation in Micro-Gravity — approach
sources.text: The final report for this investigation introduces the simulation and modeling methodology, followed by a description of the flow geometry and the parameter space under consideration.The differences in the wake geometry attributable to buoyancy for the lower of two flow speeds was examined. Instantaneous scalar fields were used to describe particle accumulation and growth in the buoyant and non-buoyant wakes that form downstream of the hot vapor source.

sources.title: Cool flames: combustion at 500–1000 K
sources.text: Cool diffusion flames have peak temperatures of about 500–1000 K. FLEX, CFI and CFI-G studied them on droplets and burners in microgravity. Limitation: Research fuels and configurations; relevance to cabin fires is an open question, not a finding.

sources.title: Microgravity and 1-g rankings of materials can disagree
sources.text: In SAFFIRE-II, 4 of 4 silicone samples (0.27–1.03 mm) had a burn length of about 0 in microgravity at 20 cm/s, while 2 of the 4 matching 1-g reference burns were complete. Flames did spread in microgravity over: PMMA, SIBAL (cotton-fiberglass fabric). Limitation: One test per configuration; single flow speed and near-normal O2.

sources.title: No partial-gravity combustion data yet
sources.text: PSI currently holds no combustion data at lunar or martian gravity. The challenge notes that microgravity and normal-gravity results can bound intermediate gravity levels, and that E-FIELD (PSI-22) mimicked partial gravity with ion-driven forces. Limitation: Bounding is not interpolation: behaviour at 1/6 g may not lie between the two cases for every metric.

sources.title: 1-g material screening is not automatically conservative
sources.text: Spacecraft material selection relies on NASA-STD-6001 Test 1, which ranks materials by 1-g behaviour. BASS and BASS-II were built on the hypothesis that, with adequate ventilation, materials burn as well if not better in microgravity than in normal gravity. Limitation: Specific materials and geometries; flow and O2 per test partly only in raw files for BASS.
